description: A six-panel TEM composite (three columns x two rows) on annealed near-rapidly solidified Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-xCr steel strips. (a), (c) and (e) are bright-field (BF) images of gamma-austenite in the 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips respectively; each carries a selected-area diffraction pattern (SADP) inset indexed to the [110] zone axis with the (001) superlattice reflection circled in red. (b), (d) and (f) are the corresponding dark-field (DF) images formed from that (001) superlattice reflection, marked "(001)" at the top right; bright nano-scale kappa-carbide particles are indicated by yellow arrows and a yellow "k" in (b) and (d). Scale bars read 500 nm in (a) and (b) and 100 nm in (c)-(f), so the 0Cr and Cr-containing strips are not imaged at the same magnification. The DF panels show the Cr-driven trend: (b) is densely speckled with fine kappa-carbide particles, (d) shows a clearly lower particle density in the 3Cr strip, and (f) for the 6Cr strip is almost featureless apart from one faint bright patch. The figure demonstrates that increasing Cr content markedly reduces the number/volume of nano-scale kappa-carbides precipitated in the annealed strips, matching the text-reported 7%/8 nm (0Cr) and 4%/4 nm (3Cr).

subfigures.description: BF TEM image of gamma-austenite in the 0Cr annealed steel strip, showing a large dark grain/thick region; inset SADP indexed along [110] with the (001) superlattice reflection circled in red; scale bar 500 nm.

DF image from the (001) superlattice reflection of kappa-carbides in the 0Cr steel strip, labelled (001) top right; densely speckled with bright nano-scale particles marked by yellow arrows and a yellow 'k'; scale bar 500 nm.
BF TEM image of gamma-austenite in the 3Cr annealed steel strip with a banded/curved contrast feature; inset SADP along [110] with the (001) reflection circled in red; scale bar 100 nm.

DF image from the (001) reflection of kappa-carbides in the 3Cr steel strip, labelled (001); bright fine particles (yellow arrows, yellow 'k') at noticeably lower density than in (b); scale bar 100 nm.
BF TEM image of gamma-austenite in the 6Cr annealed steel strip showing dislocation/banded substructure; inset SADP along [110] with (001) circled in red; scale bar 100 nm.

DF image from the (001) reflection of kappa-carbides in the 6Cr steel strip, labelled (001); the field is essentially featureless except one faint diffuse bright patch, with no arrowed kappa-carbide particles; scale bar 100 nm.

observations.observation: The figure is a six-panel TEM composite laid out as three columns by two rows: (a)-(c) on top and (d)-(f) below.
Panels (a), (c) and (e) are bright-field images; panels (b), (d) and (f) are dark-field images labelled '(001)' in their top-right corner.
Each BF panel (a), (c) and (e) contains an inset selected-area diffraction pattern labelled [110] with one reflection circled in red and annotated 001.
In (b) and (d) the bright nano-scale particles are indicated by yellow arrows together with a yellow 'k' label; no such arrows appear in (f).
Scale bars read 500 nm in (a) and (b) and 100 nm in (c), (d), (e) and (f).
The DF image (f) of the 6Cr strip is essentially featureless apart from one faint diffuse bright patch, indicating very few kappa-carbide particles.
The bright-particle density in the DF images decreases in the order (b) > (d) > (f), i.e. with increasing Cr content of the strip.

The caption states (a), (c) and (e) are BF images of gamma-austenite in the 0Cr, 3Cr and 6Cr steel strips and (b), (d) and (f) are DF images from the (001) superlattice reflection of the kappa-carbides in those same strips.
The citing text states that superlattice reflection spots appear in the SADP along the [110] zone axis taken from the gamma-austenite.

The citing text states a measured kappa-carbide volume fraction of 7% with an average size of 8 nm for the annealed 0Cr steel strip and 4% with 4 nm for the annealed 3Cr steel strip; no such numbers are printed on the figure.
The citing text concludes that Cr addition significantly decreases the size and number of kappa-carbides in the annealed strips and that higher Cr content gives less kappa-carbide precipitation.
Because (a)/(b) are at 500 nm scale while (c)-(f) are at 100 nm, the 0Cr panels cannot be compared with the Cr-containing panels at equal magnification from the pixels alone.

unreadable_items: inset SADPs in (a), (c) and (e): individual diffraction spots other than the circled 001 reflection are too small/low-contrast to index reliably
panel (f): no individual kappa-carbide particles resolvable, so no particle size can be read from the pixels
